experiments.scope: Complete 40-round SHA-256 on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family; bounded distinguished-point birthday search targeting the low 16 bits of the final digest (256 organizer trials, max 160 evaluations/trial, dp_bits=1), plus deterministic self-test of the 43,548-gate Walk-B bit-sliced kernel, 860-register Reverse-DAG zero-move allocator, 1,249-op 2-lane SIMD RecProg, and 80-digit Lemma 2 + Gamma(2F+3) ledger.
experiments.hypothesis: The bounded distinguished-point birthday search on the 64-byte W[0..7]-prefix family recovers distinct message pairs colliding on the low 16 bits of complete 40-round SHA-256 at the random-function DP birthday rate, while the bit-sliced Walk-B kernel matches complete 40-round SHA-256 on all 256 lanes.

experiments.scope: Complete 40-round SHA-256 on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family; fixed-budget birthday collision projection at width w=14 bits (256 organizer trials, budget M=127 evaluations/trial, random-function model prediction P = 1 - exp(-127^2 / (2 * 2^14)) = 0.3887).
experiments.hypothesis: Under H1, the empirical collision frequency on the low 14 bits of complete 40-round SHA-256 across 256 independent trials at budget M=127 matches the random-function birthday prediction of approximately 0.39.
